newsitem.title: FRANCE: Finland takes lion's share of EU barley sale.
newsitem.headline: Finland takes lion's share of EU barley sale.

text.p: Barley licences granted by the European Union on Thursday were taken mostly in Finland, followed by France, French cereals figures showed.
They showed 50,000 tonnes of the 70,000 tonnes awarded for export from the free market went to traders who bid through Finland. The rest went through France.
The EU awarded at a tender 70,000 tonnes of barley for export at a maximum refund of 14.92 Ecus per tonne.
It also set a standing or daily refund of zero for barley expoprts, a move seen as easing exports to the Middle East.
All of the 105,000 tonnes of wheat awarded, at a maximum refund of 0.87 Ecus, was to meet demand for refunds in France.
An award of 1,000 tonnes of rye at a refund of 23.19 Ecxus per tonne went through Denmark.
